title: Antisymmetric Dynamical Spin Correlations: Spin-Space-Group Constraints and Frequency-Moment Sum Rules
abstract: Polarized inelastic neutron scattering probes the handedness of magnetic excitations through the spin-component-antisymmetric part of the dynamical spin-structure-factor tensor. We derive its symmetry constraints under unitary and antiunitary residual operations of magnetic space groups and spin-space groups. These constraints determine the allowed tensor components, their parity under momentum reversal, and symmetry-enforced nodes. We then introduce the corresponding antisymmetric commutator spectral function and derive exact zero-temperature sum rules for its frequency moments. The zeroth moment is fixed by the uniform magnetization. For Heisenberg or XXZ exchange Hamiltonians, the first moment of the $xy$ component is fixed by a momentum-weighted static vector chirality. For compensated collinear antiferromagnets, the antisymmetric dynamical structure factor is forbidden when inversion or a translation relates the opposite-spin sublattices. In rotation-related altermagnets, however, an $xy$ component that is even under momentum reversal is allowed at generic wave vectors. Finite antisymmetric spectral weight can therefore coexist with vanishing zeroth and first moments of the commutator spectral function. In a planar helix, by contrast, a residual antiunitary spin-space-group symmetry makes the allowed $xy$ component odd under momentum reversal. Its first moment is generally nonzero and is fixed by a momentum-weighted static vector chirality through the first-moment sum rule. Linear spin-wave calculations for representative altermagnetic and helical models explicitly realize these symmetry and sum-rule constraints.
summary: This theoretical work establishes fundamental symmetry constraints and precise frequency-moment sum rules governing the antisymmetric part of the dynamical spin structure factor. By analyzing these constraints using magnetic space groups, the authors predict which types of magnetic excitations are allowed or forbidden in various ordered magnets like helices and antiferromagnets. This provides powerful diagnostic tools for interpreting inelastic neutron scattering data.
main_problem: The paper derives symmetry constraints and exact zero-temperature sum rules for the spin-component-antisymmetric part of the dynamical spin-structure-factor tensor.
main_result: These symmetries dictate selection rules for magnetic excitations, allowing finite spectral weight even when zeroth or first frequency moments vanish under specific crystal/spin symmetries.
method: The analysis uses group theory applied to residual unitary and antiunitary operations of magnetic space groups and spin-space groups, combined with linear spin-wave calculations.
model_or_system: The framework is applied to general magnetic systems, including collinear antiferromagnets, rotation-related altermagnets, and planar helical magnets (e.g., on a triangular lattice).
key_observables: Antisymmetric dynamical spin-structure-factor tensor ($C_{\alpha eta}(\mathbf{q}, \omega)$), commutator spectral function $A_{\alpha eta}^{	ext{as}}(\mathbf{q}, \omega)$, and its frequency moments ($M^0, M^1$).
important_parameters: Zero temperature ($T=0$), momentum ($\mathbf{q}$), and the specific symmetry operations (unitary/antiunitary).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on deriving constraints from residual space group symmetries; some calculations use linear spin-wave theory approximations.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes, but the text discusses explicit realizations of these constraints via LSWT for helical magnets and general symmetry rules for different magnetic types.
paper_structure: The paper first defines the antisymmetric DSF, then derives general symmetry constraints using space groups, establishes moment sum rules (zeroth and first moments), and finally applies this framework to specific models like collinear antiferromagnets and planar helices.
why_interesting: While focused on magnetism, the rigorous application of group theory symmetries to derive exact spectral properties and sum rules is a powerful general technique applicable to any quantum many-body system where symmetry dictates observable selection rules.
